column1: ref-05-02|Buyer-insured Karim 40; hypertension diagnosed 2022, medicine ongoing; new policy proposed 1 Oct 2026; no offer accepted.|Has the condition been declared, and has the insurer separately specified acceptance, waiting and any loading?|The condition is declared in the proposal; the insurer has requested tests and has not quoted final terms.|Ongoing treatment falls within the preserved regulatory PED definition. Declaration is necessary information but not acceptance or proof of a loading. Record eligibility, extra premium and waiting as separate proposed/accepted outcomes. Do not claim all hypertension buyers are refused or that declaration automatically gives immediate cover.|P5,N22,N9|Final underwriting terms and selected product waiting/applicability remain missing; New India's internal PED-duration conflict must not be silently resolved.

ref-05-03|Buyer-insured Karim 40; asthma for 6 years, uses prescribed inhaler intermittently, last consultation Jun 2026; no hospital admissions.|Was there recent medical advice or treatment even without admission?|Yes, the inhaler is prescribed and was renewed in June.|No hospitalisation does not imply no PED. The regulator's lookback includes physician advice/treatment. Record intermittent treatment, dates and declared status without inventing severity or loading; apply the selected wording and accepted terms before an eligibility decision.|P5,N22|Actual insurer acceptance, exact asthma disclosure and current product conditions missing.

ref-05-04|Buyer-insured Karim 40; thyroid medicine prescribed monthly; salesperson said minor conditions need not be mentioned; application pending.|What does the original proposal ask, and has the medicine been disclosed?|Not disclosed yet; I have no copy of the full proposal question.|Do not recommend omission based on perceived seriousness. Retain the condition/medicine and request the actual disclosure question, then update the proposal information through the insurer's process. A PED lookback does not limit broader questions. Diagnosis, treatment, disclosure and underwriting outcome remain separate.|P5,N9,N37|Exact proposal question and insurer-recorded disclosure/update absent; no assurance that omission is immaterial.

ref-05-05|Buyer Karim 40; mother 67 with diabetes and hypertension, current treatment; needs Hospital S, Jaipur branch; no accepted offer.|Are both conditions disclosed and is the exact branch supported under each candidate?|Both reported here; neither insurer confirmation nor branch listing supplied.|Use person-specific disclosures for both conditions, not one chronic-disease flag. Evaluate each waiting/exclusion/underwriting term and the branch independently. A candidate acceptable for one condition can remain uncertain for the other or fail the mandatory hospital requirement. Keep missing evidence distinct from supported medical rejection.|P5,I6,I31,N28|Two-condition acceptance and exact branch/network-option evidence absent.

ref-05-06|Buyer-insured Karim 40; proposal 1 Sep 2026 said no diabetes; physician diagnosed 8 Sep; proposed inception 1 Oct; no issued policy.|Has the new diagnosis been communicated before the insurer's decision and start date?|Not yet; I thought the earlier form was final.|Preserve the original application as history and the later diagnosis as a new dated disclosure; do not overwrite what was known on 1 September. An unaccepted proposal is not cover. Seek insurer acknowledgment and revised acceptance terms before relying on 1 October commencement; don't treat the old negative assertion as current.|P5,N9,N37|Insurer acknowledgment, revised offer and actual inception missing. A current diagnosis cannot be hidden by freezing an earlier form.

ref-05-07|Buyer-insured Karim 40; new base policy quote; brochure mentions chronic add-on with shorter wait; option not selected; diabetes ongoing.|Does the quote explicitly include the add-on and its person-specific acceptance?|No; only the public brochure mentions it.|An available optional grant does not change the base waiting rule. Retain option availability, requested selection, actual selection, rider revision and accepted insured scope separately. Show the current quote fails to establish the desired earlier-cover feature and obtain a corrected offer; do not generalize the brochure to every buyer.|I7,N9,N37|Authentic add-on terms, eligibility, price and selected acceptance missing; no shortened waiting period established.

ref-05-08|Buyer-insured Karim 40; diabetes medicines 2000/month, routine tests 6000/year; wants New India AS hospital plus outpatient cover.|Are these standalone outpatient costs or expenses related to an admissible admission?|Standalone ongoing costs; no admission.|Annual expected OPD spend is 30000. New India's OPD exclusion means the hospitalisation grant does not establish reimbursement of that routine spend. Separate catastrophe protection from the recurring-expense requirement and investigate original-backed OPD alternatives. Do not recast routine prescriptions as pre/post-hospital expenses without a linked admission.|N27,N7,N8|Source-backed suitable OPD option and quote missing; 30000 is an expense estimate, not a payable benefit.

ref-05-09|Buyer-insured Karim, 40; diabetes is disclosed in an unaccepted personal offer; the offer summary states a 20% disease co-pay, while marketing states zero co-pay; no full endorsement is available.|What exact personal clause defines affected claims and the percentage base, and was it accepted?|Only the offer summary; I have not accepted it.|Keep the general product assertion and personal offer distinct. Do not override the owner-specific restriction with marketing or apply it to other customers. A hypothetical 100000 admissible diabetes claim at 20% would mean 20000 cost share, but actual scope/order require the endorsement. Proposed terms are not yet accepted terms.|N28,N31,N37|Exact offer wording, disease attribution, percentage base and consent/acceptance absent.

ref-05-10|Buyer-insured Karim 40; abnormal glucose blood test 9 Sep 2026; no formal diagnosis; proposal due 10 Sep; follow-up scheduled.|Was diabetes diagnosed or only an abnormal finding reported, and what does the proposal ask about investigations?|Only a finding; doctor requested repeat testing.|Store an abnormal test and pending investigation as reported facts without labeling diabetes or recording a clean history. Ask the relevant proposal questions about symptoms, tests and advice; preserve the later result as a revision. No diagnosis, acceptance or rate should be inferred from the number alone.|P5,N9,N37|Original proposal questions, clinical interpretation and underwriting decision absent.

ref-06-01|Buyer-insured Noor 45; cancer therapy ended Sep 2023; ongoing follow-up Jun 2026; new indemnity policy requested Oct 2026.|What cancer type/status and current follow-up are documented, and is there an underwriting offer?|No recurrence reported; oncologist follow-up continues; no offer.|Time since treatment alone cannot establish either absence of PED or acceptance. The recent follow-up is relevant to lookback/disclosure. Compare medical-expense contracts and exact recurrence exclusions/limits; do not substitute a fixed first-diagnosis benefit. Request original acceptance conditions before any shortlist.|P5,I6,N28|Cancer-specific facts, current medical report, source-backed suitable products and offers missing.

ref-06-02|Buyer Noor 45; father 69 had stent 2024; current cardiac medicine; offered cardiac-specific product but payout type unknown.|Does it reimburse medical expenses or pay a fixed sum only on a defined event?|The summary says cardiac cover; no wording supplied.|A cardiac label does not establish indemnity for an already treated condition. The regulations distinguish loss-based indemnity from fixed-event benefits. Identify product/UIN, event definition, existing-disease acceptance, waits and treatment limits; keep father's history separate from buyer. Do not count a diagnosis benefit as hospital-bill cover.|P7,P5,I6|Exact product type, event definition and individual offer missing; no cardiac-treatment payment established.

ref-06-03|Buyer-insured Noor 45; chronic kidney disease with dialysis planned three times weekly; New India AS considered; visits under 24 hours.|Is the procedure listed daycare at an eligible facility, and what waiting/acceptance applies?|Haemodialysis; no accepted policy yet; clinic status unknown.|The preserved daycare list includes haemodialysis, so lack of overnight stay alone is not a rejection basis. Join that listing to facility definition, admission/OPD distinction, PED and other waits, limits and acceptance. A listed procedure does not itself prove immediate payment for established kidney disease.|N45,N4,N22,N23|Facility evidence, accepted CKD terms and applicable waiting resolution absent.

ref-06-04|Buyer-insured Noor 45; hospital discharge 20 Aug 2026; provisional diagnosis; final report pending; proposal 10 Sep.|What symptoms, investigations and treatment were documented even though diagnosis is pending?|Records show treatment and unresolved cause; no final diagnosis.|Keep provisional findings, admission and pending diagnosis separately, with dates and provenance. Unknown diagnosis is not no illness, and a later result should append a correction rather than rewrite history. Obtain original proposal questions and insurer decision; do not infer a diagnosis to force a product match.|P5,N9,N37|Final clinical interpretation and insurer assessment absent; underwriting cannot be represented as completed.

ref-06-05|Buyer Noor 45; mother 68 with cancer history and diabetes; existing SI 500000; requests increase 500000; recent treatment Jul 2026.|Which conditions are currently accepted and which amount is old versus newly requested?|Old schedule available in principle, but no individual clauses supplied; increase pending.|Assess each condition against the old accepted terms and the requested layer separately. Increasing SI can start new waiting/moratorium clocks for the increase; neither existing payment history nor one accepted condition proves the other is covered. Keep future accepted options distinct from current rights.|N28,N38,P11,P5|Individual old terms, two-condition evidence and increase offer missing.

ref-06-06|Buyer-insured Noor, 45; a new offer reportedly excludes recurrence of past cancer; other hospital cover appears available; acceptance is pending.|What does recurrence mean in the exact exclusion and which insured/benefits does it affect?|Only a one-line summary, not accepted.|A restricted offer is not full cancer protection and not necessarily no cover for every other illness. Preserve the proposed exclusion text and scope, identify the unmet priority, and compare alternatives without assuming the exclusion is valid or applies universally. Do not present it as accepted.|N28,N37,P17|Exact recurrence definition, legal/applicability review and alternative offers missing.

ref-06-07|Buyer-insured Noor 45; surgery 2012, no follow-up since 2013; application question reportedly asks any lifetime surgery.|Can you supply the exact proposal wording rather than only the PED definition?|I read the question as asking whether I have ever undergone surgery. The old operation was successful; I have not supplied the original proposal page.|Answer the actual lifetime question; a 36-month PED lookback is a different concept and does not justify denying the reported surgery. Preserve historical event and current treatment status separately. Request insurer-recorded disclosure and assessment without inventing a PED classification or extra charge.|P5,N9,N37|Original proposal question and insurer acknowledgment missing; do not narrow its scope through unrelated lookback rules.

ref-06-08|Buyer-insured Noor 45; biopsy taken 8 Sep 2026; result due 15 Sep; seeks immediate purchase 10 Sep.|Are the symptoms, test and pending result disclosed, and has cover actually been accepted?|Not yet; I hoped to finish before the result.|Pending investigation is material context, not a negative diagnosis. Retain dates and update through the insurer; do not advise rushing acceptance to conceal a finding or promise funding for the current episode. Exact proposal questions and acceptance control any offer.|P5,N9,N37|Clinical result, complete disclosure and accepted contract absent.

ref-06-09|Buyer-insured Noor 45; existing indemnity policy; major claim paid Jul 2026; renewal Oct 2026; worried about rejection.|Has the insurer actually refused renewal, changed portfolio price or only asked for the requested increase?|No refusal; just concern after a large claim.|The regulator says prior claims alone do not justify ordinary indemnity renewal denial, with stated exceptions and withdrawal/moratorium context. Do not invent a refusal or personal claims loading. Distinguish renewal, portfolio pricing, a benefit policy that terminates on payout, and any requested increase.|I16,P12,P14,P15|Actual renewal offer/current terms needed for price or refusal assessment; the concern itself is not an adverse insurer decision.

ref-06-10|Buyer-insured Noor 45 is recipient; sister 42 donor; proposed transplant; Star Gold considered; costs include screening, donor surgery and later complication.|Which person incurs each bill and is the recipient transplantation admissible under the policy?|Recipient eligibility not yet established; all three donor categories appear in estimate.|Star's donor grant depends on payable recipient transplantation and available SI; donor screening and post-donation complications are excluded under that grant. Keep each person and expense category separate. Do not infer the donor's own policy covers them or count an excluded cost under recipient surgery merely by combining bills.|S11,N9|Recipient acceptance/waits, original itemized estimate and any donor's separate cover missing.

ref-07-01|Buyer-insured Esha 30; needs inpatient mental-health treatment; product not selected; no full medical offer.|Is the need inpatient admission or outpatient counselling, and what exact treatment is advised?|Inpatient admission; no substance-related diagnosis reported.|The regulator requires relevant product offerings and statutory compliance, not universal acceptance under one product. Obtain the exact indemnity benefit, facility, limits and exclusion terms. Do not extend a substance-treatment exclusion to all psychiatric care or promise blanket cover because mental health is mentioned.|I6,I37,E11|Specific original product, clinical/setting facts and underwriting terms absent.

ref-07-02|Buyer-insured Esha, 30; physical disability since childhood; seeks a medical-expense policy; reports 18000/year but has not clarified whether this is income or the insurance budget.|What disability and support needs matter, is the proposed product indemnity insurance, and does the reported amount mean income or premium budget?|No exact product is identified; wheelchair access matters. The meaning of the reported amount still needs clarification.|Separate medical eligibility from physical access and affordability. The regulator's model-product obligation does not itself prove this person's acceptance or every benefit. Locate the specific original/model parameters and applicable offer; do not assume blanket denial from disability status.|I37,I6,I31|Specific product/model circular dependencies, individual acceptance and accessible provider observations are missing. The reported annual amount must be clarified before affordability is assessed.

ref-07-03|Buyer Esha 30; son 6 internal congenital condition; New India AS proposed; surgery 2 months after fresh inception.|Is the anomaly internal or external and do any continuity credits or permanent exclusions apply?|Internal; no prior cover; treatment known before purchase.|New India's specific list includes internal congenital anomalies with 24-month wait; overlapping PED and accepted exclusions also need review. A fresh policy two months old does not satisfy that stipulated wait. Do not replace internal with external or conclude every congenital condition is permanently excluded.|N24,N23,N22|Applicable PED conflict resolution and accepted individual terms absent; no imminent surgery funding established.

ref-07-04|Buyer-insured Esha 30; HIV diagnosed 2024, ongoing treatment; wants bill reimbursement not lump sum; no offer.|Is the candidate an indemnity model product and what HIV-specific terms are actually provided?|Only an advertisement; waiting period not shown.|The model-product duty and benefit-type distinction support requesting the actual medical-expense wording rather than assuming a fixed diagnosis benefit is suitable. Preserve disclosed HIV status with consent/ownership controls; compare waits, limits and acceptance from originals. No blanket approval or refusal follows from the label.|I37,P7,I6|Model circular/product wording, limits, waits and underwriting acceptance missing.

ref-07-05|Buyer Esha 30; father 66 has disability and diabetes; needs wheelchair-accessible Hospital T branch; no accepted quote.|Are medical acceptance and physical accessibility each documented for this exact branch?|Neither; only insurer network name appears.|A network match is not accessibility evidence, and disability acceptance does not settle diabetes terms. Retain dated branch accessibility, network/excluded status and person-condition acceptance independently. Require all material constraints before calling a candidate suitable; absent evidence is uncertainty, not automatic exclusion.|I31,I37,P5|Accessible-branch observation, both-condition terms and quote absent.

ref-07-06|Buyer-insured Esha 30; seeks weekly counselling, not admission; brochure mentions mental health; New India AS example.|Does the exact benefit include outpatient sessions or only eligible inpatient/daycare treatment?|No outpatient clause located.|An inpatient mental-health description does not establish counselling reimbursement. New India's OPD exclusion illustrates the setting dependency; do not substitute a broad disease label for a service grant. Find an applicable OPD benefit, visit cap, provider and access rules before pricing expected counselling spend.|N27,E11,P7|Specific counselling grant and quote absent; general mental-health availability does not resolve OPD payment.

ref-07-07|Buyer-insured Esha 30; external congenital anomaly; optional cover mentioned but selection unknown; surgery later planned.|What exact condition does the rider cover, and is it selected/accepted for you?|No rider PDF or accepted selection supplied.|Keep the external classification, any reported general exclusion and the proposed rider separate. An applicable rider can create an exception only within its exact scope; marketing alone cannot remove an exclusion. Request the base clause, rider and condition-specific underwriting terms, including any wait or cap. No general exclusion or exception is established from the information supplied.|N28,N37,I7|Authentic general/rider clauses and personal acceptance missing; no exception established.

ref-07-08|Buyer-insured Esha 30; comparing psychiatric admission and substance-related rehabilitation; asks whether both same exclusion.|What treatment purpose and diagnosis apply to each episode?|One psychiatric admission without substance cause; another programme explicitly treats alcohol dependence.|New India's 7.9 is a substance-related treatment/consequences exclusion, not a textual exclusion of all mental care. Assess each episode's purpose, connected exclusions and benefit setting separately. Do not infer causation from co-occurring diagnoses; no payment for the unrelated episode is established by absence of that one exclusion.|E7,N27,E11|Episode-specific clinical attribution and full applicable product benefits/waits missing.

ref-07-09|Buyer-insured Esha 30; two advertised HIV/disability products; one SI 500000, other 1000000; no originals.|Are both indemnity and do they have the same treatment limits, waiting periods and accepted conditions?|Unknown; sales pages only show product names and SI.|A shared category label and larger SI do not prove equivalent scope. Obtain each exact product/UIN and model-minimum dependencies, then compare condition/setting limits and acceptance. Retain every uncertain dimension; do not rank on SI while assuming missing limits are unlimited.|I37,P7,I6|Both original bundles, condition-specific limits and personal offers missing.

ref-07-10|Buyer-insured Esha 30; general disease benefit appears positive; individual schedule has conflicting exclusion; issued terms unavailable here.|Can you provide both exact clauses, affected person and endorsement effective dates?|I only have summaries and do not know which applies.|Retain both assertions and their provenance; do not impose a generic document rank without checking lawful scope, effective dates and express precedence. A personal exclusion must not become a public product exclusion. Block the conflicting claim conclusion and identify the exact documents needed for resolution.|N28,N37,N9|Actual schedule/endorsement/general benefit and precedence/legal applicability absent.

ref-08-01|Buyer-insured Kavya, 29; reports being 24 weeks pregnant, with the date of that observation unspecified; delivery is expected Jan 2027; new Star Gold cover proposed Oct 2026; no prior continuity.|Have both spouses been insured for the required period, and is this existing cover or a new proposal?|Fresh policy for both spouses; no continuity credit.|Star Gold delivery benefit has 12-month waiting plus both-spouse/in-force conditions and limits. A January delivery after fresh October inception does not satisfy the stipulated wait. Do not promise cover for this pregnancy from a new purchase or general maternity label. Investigate genuinely existing applicable cover separately.|S9,S10,S21|No accepted existing qualifying contract or explicit exception is supplied. Confirm the date of the reported pregnancy stage and expected delivery date; the proposed new cover does not establish payment for this delivery.

ref-08-02|Buyer Kavya, 29, and spouse, 31; planning for delivery about 2 years away; comparing Star Gold and New India AS; no quotes.|Is maternity essential, and what actual commencement and delivery dates should be compared?|Essential; assume purchase 1 Oct 2026 and delivery 1 Nov 2028 for illustration.|Star Gold has a conditional delivery benefit with 12-month wait, both spouses and lifetime/per-period limits. New India AS excludes routine maternity subject to specific exceptions. The assumed timeline alone meets a 12-month duration but does not establish full Star acceptance or benefit availability at the future event. Compare original restrictions and price, not just wait length.|S9,S10,N26|Actual offers, spouse-specific continuity, lifetime delivery count and future applicable terms need evidence.

ref-08-03|Buyer-insured Kavya 29; personal policy summary says normal cap 30000 and caesarean cap 50000; expects delivery; actual mode unknown.|Are the caps alternatives per delivery and is there a combined family/year limit?|Only summary available; childbirth mode not yet known.|Retain procedure-specific alternatives and actual event classification. Do not add 30000 and 50000 to create 80000 cover without an explicit combined grant. A stated 50k Star Gold delivery cap is a different product structure, not evidence for this unnamed split-cap contract. Obtain exact terms before a payment estimate.|S9,N9|Original normal/caesarean cap clauses, shared limits and accepted personal terms absent; numbers remain customer-reported.

ref-08-04|Buyer-insured Kavya 29; planning IVF; New India AS and Star Gold maternity advertisements seen.|Does the selected original expressly cover assisted reproduction rather than only delivery?|No IVF rider or grant located.|New India's infertility exclusion expressly lists assisted reproduction including IVF. Star's maternity grant should not be generalized to all fertility treatment; its exclusions are separate dependencies. Reject the claim that a maternity label establishes IVF cover, while keeping any independently evidenced alternative product open.|E6,S21,N9|Source-backed IVF alternative/rider and personal offer absent; no IVF payment established.

ref-08-05|Buyer Kavya 29, spouse 31; hypothetical Star Gold; wants delivery and newborn NICU; itemized mother bill 60000, newborn 80000.|Are the expenses attributed to mother or newborn and does a separate newborn benefit apply?|No separate newborn cover supplied; both costs on one hospital estimate.|Star's delivery grant and newborn exclusion require separate benefit decisions. Do not put newborn NICU into the mother's delivery cap or count one expense twice. The mother's limit/wait and lifetime conditions also need verification; the newborn bill is not supported merely because maternity is granted.|S9,S10,S22|Actual accepted continuity, delivery count and any independent newborn cover absent.

ref-08-06|Buyer Kavya 29, spouse 31; Star Gold first start 1 Oct 2025; uninterrupted both spouses; expected delivery 29 Sep 2026; actual date unknown.|What is the actual delivery date and has the 12-month wait completed under the policy's event rule?|Not delivered yet; estimated date may move by days.|Expected date cannot decide an actual-event boundary. At 29 September the stated 12-month anniversary has not arrived; at 1 October it has, subject to exact commencement/time interpretation and other conditions. Keep the outcome conditional until the actual event and policy records establish the boundary; do not round months to 360 days.|S9,S10|Actual delivery event, exact time-boundary treatment and complete accepted benefit conditions not yet established.

ref-08-07|Buyer Kavya, 34; expecting a third child; considering the Star Gold delivery benefit; prior births include an uninsured event and an event for which a claim was paid.|Does the lifetime restriction count all deliveries or only claims covered under this benefit, and what original history exists?|One previous birth was uninsured; exact clause interpretation not confirmed.|The Star original says maximum 2 deliveries in the insured person's lifetime. Do not substitute number of children or paid claims for the stated event count without resolving interpretation, including twins/miscarriage history where relevant. Preserve actual deliveries, claims and coverage periods separately and seek a supported application to this third event.|S9,S10|Complete delivery history and interpretation of the lifetime restriction need adjudication; no third-delivery promise.

ref-08-08|Buyer Vikram, 31, has held a policy for 3 years; adding his spouse Kavya, 29, is proposed in Sep 2026; pregnancy planned Oct 2026; Star Gold is the candidate.|When is the spouse's addition accepted and how does the both-spouse waiting condition apply?|The addition has not been accepted. I assumed Vikram's 3 years would automatically provide credit for Kavya.|Existing member history is not automatic new-member credit. Star delivery requires both spouses covered/in force and a waiting condition whose person/policy application must be resolved with addition terms. Preserve each member's inception and accepted credit; do not reuse the older member's clock without evidence.|S9,N37,N38|Accepted addition, specific waiting-credit treatment and maternal eligibility missing.

ref-08-09|Buyer-insured Kavya 29; doctor reports possible ectopic pregnancy; New India AS existing policy; routine maternity excluded.|Is ectopic pregnancy confirmed and what admissible hospital treatment is proposed?|Diagnosis pending; urgent assessment recommended.|The maternity exclusion contains an ectopic exception, so blanket maternity denial would be wrong. An exception to one exclusion is not a complete benefit grant: confirm diagnosis, eligible admission, waits and other limits. Do not broaden the exception to every pregnancy complication or delay medical care for an insurance conclusion.|N26,N10,N23|Confirmed diagnosis and full applicable claim conditions absent; keep the exception and uncertainty explicit.

ref-08-10|Buyer Kavya 29, spouse 31; annual budget 25000; base quote 22000; maternity option price unknown, selection unknown.|Is maternity mandatory, and is the option included in the quoted 22000?|Mandatory; no selection line or add-on price.|The current offer does not establish the required benefit or affordability. Unknown option cost is not zero; obtain rider terms, accepted selection, waits, delivery/newborn limits and final quote. Base premium 22000 leaves 3000 budget headroom arithmetically, but cannot prove the option fits it.|I7,N9,S9|Authentic applicable rider and all-in personal price absent; do not mark the base quote suitable for the maternity requirement.
